title: Digital and Analog Signals
seo_title: Digital Signals Worksheets: Bits, Binary, File Sizes and Analog vs Digital (Physics)
standard_text: Evaluate questions about the advantages of using a digital transmission and storage of information.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on digital and analog signals (NGSS HS-PS4-2): bits and binary, 2ⁿ values, file sizes, download times and the advantages and drawbacks of digital data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Digital resists noise and copies perfectly, but sampling, hacking and old formats are risks.
body_html:
How to think about it

Digital information is stored and sent as bits (0s and 1s).

  • n bits can show 2n different values. 1 byte = 8 bits.
  • Advantages: resists noise, copies perfectly, can be compressed, encrypted and error-checked.
  • Drawbacks: sampling misses some detail, data can be hacked or lost, and formats go out of date.
Example

How many values with 4 bits?

24

Answer: 16

Example

100 MB file at 50 Mbps?

100 × 8 = 800 Mb

800 ÷ 50

Answer: 16 s

Common mistakes

  • Thinking 8 bits store only 8 values.
  • Mixing up megabytes (MB) and megabits (Mb).
  • Thinking digital has no drawbacks.

faq.q: What is the difference between analog and digital signals?
faq.a: An analog signal changes smoothly. A digital signal uses separate values, usually bits (0 and 1).

faq.q: How many values can n bits store?
faq.a: 2ⁿ values. For example, 8 bits (1 byte) can store 256 different values.

faq.q: What are the advantages of digital signals?
faq.a: They resist noise, can be copied perfectly, compressed, encrypted and checked for errors.
